Bank of India is a state-owned commercial bank headquartered in Mumbai, founded in 1906 and nationalised in 1969. It offers retail, corporate, SME, agricultural and international banking through thousands of domestic branches plus overseas branches in major financial centres including London, Singapore and Hong Kong. Customers range from individuals to large corporates and government bodies; revenue comes from lending margins and fees. The Government of India is the majority shareholder and the shares are listed on the NSE and BSE. Well known in India, little visibility elsewhere.

Bank of Jiangsu is a Chinese joint-stock commercial bank headquartered in Nanjing, Jiangsu province, listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. It provides corporate lending, retail banking, wealth management, treasury and financial markets services, mainly across Jiangsu and the Yangtze River Delta, with branches in other major Chinese cities. Customers are local enterprises, SMEs and individuals, and income comes from loan interest and fees. It is a large regional lender by Chinese standards. Regional brand with low international consumer awareness.

Bank of Montreal (BMO Financial Group) is one of Canada's five largest banks, founded in 1817 and headquartered in Toronto, with a registered office in Montreal. It offers personal and commercial banking, wealth management and capital markets, with a large US presence after acquiring Bank of the West in 2023 and BMO Harris Bank. It serves millions of retail and corporate clients and earns money from lending spreads, fees and investment services. Listed on the TSX and NYSE as BMO. Strong consumer brand in Canada and the US Midwest, and an existing sports sponsor (BMO Field, golf).

BB Energy is a London-based independent energy trading company, active in trading, chartering, logistics and storage of oil products, fuel oil, crude and related commodities worldwide, with offices in London, Dubai, Singapore, Geneva and Houston. Customers are refiners, utilities, shipping firms and national oil companies, and it earns from trading margins and logistics services. It is privately held and a large commodities trader by volume. B2B, little public brand awareness.

Blue Owl Capital is a New York-based alternative asset manager listed on the NYSE (OWL), formed in 2021 through a SPAC merger of Owl Rock and Dyal Capital. It manages well over 200 billion dollars across direct lending, GP strategic capital, and real assets such as net lease and digital infrastructure including data centres. Clients are institutions, insurers and wealthy individuals, and it earns management and performance fees. Blue Owl has taken sports-related stakes in minority team-ownership funds. B2B financial brand with low consumer awareness.

Booz Allen Hamilton is a management and technology consulting firm headquartered in McLean, Virginia, founded in 1914 and listed on the NYSE (BAH). It sells consulting, cyber, analytics, AI and engineering services overwhelmingly to the US federal government, including defence, intelligence and civilian agencies, with roughly 35,000 employees and annual revenue above 11 billion dollars. Revenue comes from government contracts. Investment firm Carlyle was a long-time major shareholder before exiting. B2B and government contractor with modest public brand awareness outside Washington.

Borr Drilling is an offshore drilling contractor that owns and operates a modern fleet of jack-up rigs, working for oil and gas majors and national oil companies in the Middle East, Southeast Asia, Mexico and West Africa. Founded in 2016, it is Bermuda-incorporated with management offices in London and Norway and is listed on the NYSE and Oslo Bors (BORR). Revenue comes from day-rate rig contracts. B2B oilfield services company with almost no consumer brand recognition.

Broadridge Financial Solutions is a fintech provider of investor communications, proxy voting, securities processing and wealth technology, spun off from ADP in 2007. Its platforms process trillions of dollars in daily trading volume for banks, broker-dealers, asset managers and public companies, with about 14,000 employees and revenue near 6.5 billion dollars. It is headquartered in Lake Success, New York, with offices worldwide, and is listed on the NYSE (BR). B2B infrastructure, little consumer brand awareness.

Brookfield Asset Management is one of the world's largest alternative asset managers, with over 1 trillion dollars of assets under management across renewable power, infrastructure, real estate, private equity and credit. Headquartered in Toronto and listed on the NYSE and TSX (BAM), it was separated from Brookfield Corporation in 2022. Clients are pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, insurers and private investors, and it earns management and carry fees. Portfolio companies include many well-known assets. Institutional brand with low consumer awareness.

BT Group is the UK's largest fixed-line and broadband and mobile network operator, headquartered in London, with roughly 100,000 employees. Consumer brands include BT, EE and Plusnet; business unit BT Business and Openreach, the national access network, serve enterprises and wholesale customers. It also offers TV including sports channels such as TNT Sports (a joint venture, formerly BT Sport). Listed on the London Stock Exchange (BT.A) with annual revenue around 20 billion pounds. Very strong UK consumer brand with a history of sports sponsorship.

Canadian Natural Resources (CNRL) is one of Canada's largest independent oil and natural gas producers, headquartered in Calgary and listed on the TSX and NYSE (CNQ). It produces over 1.3 million barrels of oil equivalent per day from oil sands (Horizon, Albian), conventional heavy oil, offshore (North Sea, Africa) and natural gas, selling mostly to refiners and marketers. Revenue is commodity sales. Founded in 1973. B2B upstream producer with limited consumer brand awareness.

Canara Bank is a large Indian public sector bank headquartered in Bengaluru, founded in 1906 and nationalised in 1969. It provides retail, corporate, agriculture and MSME banking across thousands of branches and ATMs in India, with branches abroad, and owns stakes in asset management and insurance joint ventures. Customers are individuals, farmers, SMEs and corporates; revenue comes from lending and fees. Government of India holds the majority and shares trade on NSE and BSE. Recognisable consumer brand in India, mainly southern regions.

Centalion is a Geneva-based energy trading firm active in crude oil, refined products and natural gas, serving refiners, traders and utilities across Europe, Africa and Asia. The reported funding figure appears to reflect large credit or debt facilities rather than equity. It earns trading margins and logistics fees. Privately held and relatively recent as an independent trader. B2B commodity trader with almost no public consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Cheniere Energy is the largest US producer of liquefied natural gas, headquartered in Houston and listed on the NYSE American (LNG). It operates the Sabine Pass terminal in Louisiana and the Corpus Christi terminal in Texas, exporting LNG to buyers across Europe, Asia and Latin America under long-term contracts. Revenue is tolling and sales to utilities, trading houses and energy majors, around 20 billion dollars annually. Founded 1996. B2B energy infrastructure with little consumer visibility.

China CITIC Bank is a major Chinese joint-stock commercial bank headquartered in Beijing, majority-owned by CITIC Group. It provides corporate and retail banking, credit cards, wealth management and cross-border finance through over 1,400 branches nationwide, and is dual-listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong. Customers are Chinese enterprises, state-linked firms and individuals; revenue comes from loan interest, card fees and treasury. Well known in China, with limited consumer awareness elsewhere.

China Construction Bank is one of China's Big Four state-owned banks and among the world's largest by assets, headquartered in Beijing and listed in Hong Kong and Shanghai. It provides corporate, retail, infrastructure and property finance, wealth management and international banking through around 14,000 domestic outlets and branches in major world cities. Customers include state enterprises, SMEs and hundreds of millions of individuals; the state fund Central Huijin is the leading shareholder. Strong brand in China and a presence in global financial rankings.

China Life Insurance is China's largest life insurer, headquartered in Beijing and majority owned by the state through China Life Insurance (Group). It sells life, health, accident and annuity products to hundreds of millions of policyholders via a vast agent network and bancassurance, and manages large investment portfolios. Listed in Hong Kong, New York and Shanghai. Revenue is premiums and investment income. Household name in China and a state-backed financial brand with limited recognition abroad.

CIBC (Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce) is one of Canada's Big Five banks, headquartered in Toronto, tracing its roots to 1867. It provides personal and business banking, credit cards, wealth management, capital markets and US commercial banking through CIBC Bank USA, serving over 10 million clients. Listed on the TSX and NYSE (CM), with revenue around 20 billion Canadian dollars. Revenue comes from lending spreads, fees and advisory work. Strong Canadian consumer brand with local sports and community sponsorships.

Citibanamex (Banco Nacional de Mexico, Banamex) is one of Mexico's largest banks, founded in 1884 and headquartered in Mexico City. It offers retail banking, credit cards, SME and corporate banking, and wealth management through hundreds of branches. It was owned by Citigroup from 2001, which announced a split in 2022 and sold a 25 percent stake to Fernando Chico Pardo in 2025 as it prepared an IPO; Banamex operates as a separate entity. Customers are Mexican individuals and businesses. Very well-known consumer brand in Mexico and historic sports sponsor.

Clean Power Alliance is a not-for-profit community choice aggregator (CCA) serving Los Angeles and Ventura County, California, buying and supplying cleaner electricity to roughly a million customer accounts in dozens of cities while Southern California Edison continues delivering power. Funded through electricity rates paid by residents and businesses, it procures renewable energy and invests in local programs. Public agency formed in 2017. Local utility brand, limited wider consumer visibility.

Clifford Capital is a Singapore-based specialist finance company providing export credit, project finance and infrastructure and marine lending to companies, especially in Asia. Founded in 2012 with Temasek among its backers, it works with insurers and banks. Customers are corporates, shipping and infrastructure firms. The listed funding amount appears to be debt raised. B2B financial institution with low public brand awareness.

CloudWalk is a Brazilian fintech headquartered in Sao Paulo that operates the InfinitePay payments business and the JIM.com platform, offering card machines, digital accounts, credit and merchant services to small and medium businesses. Founded in 2013, it has raised well over 300 million dollars from investors including Valor Capital and Redpoint, with a valuation above 2 billion dollars. Revenue comes from transaction fees, credit and account services. Strong brand among Brazilian small merchants, expanding in Latin America and the US.

CNX Resources is a Pittsburgh-area natural gas producer based in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania, with operations in the Appalachian Basin including the Marcellus and Utica shales, and is listed on the NYSE (CNX). It produces around 600 billion cubic feet-equivalent annually, selling gas to utilities, marketers and industrial buyers, and also runs midstream and technology ventures. Revenue is natural gas sales and hedging. Origins trace to a coal and gas business founded in the 19th century. B2B energy producer with limited public awareness.

Comcast is a US media and technology conglomerate headquartered in Philadelphia and listed on Nasdaq (CMCSA). It owns Xfinity broadband and cable, NBCUniversal (NBC, Peacock, Universal Pictures, theme parks, Telemundo), Sky in Europe, and the Versant cable spin-off planned for 2026. It has over 30 million broadband customers and revenue near 120 billion dollars. Money comes from subscriptions, advertising, film and theme park admissions. Huge consumer brands and a major sports broadcaster, including NFL, Premier League and the Olympics, so a likely media partner.

Comision Federal de Electricidad (CFE) is Mexico's state-owned electricity utility, headquartered in Mexico City, generating, transmitting and distributing power to around 48 million customers. It operates hydro, thermal, geothermal, wind and nuclear stations, and also sells fuel and telecom services. Revenue comes from electricity tariffs and government support; it is a government-owned productive enterprise created in 1937. Very well-known public utility brand in Mexico with low relevance as a commercial sponsor.

Commonwealth Fusion Systems is a Massachusetts-based fusion energy company spun out of MIT in 2018, based in Devens. It is building the SPARC tokamak using high-temperature superconducting magnets and plans the ARC power plant, with Google as a customer and Eni a major investor. It has raised roughly 3 billion dollars from investors including Bill Gates's Breakthrough Energy, Tiger Global and Google, making it among the best-funded fusion startups. Pre-revenue deep-tech with high profile in climate and technology media.

Commonwealth LNG is a developer of a planned liquefied natural gas export terminal at Cameron Parish, Louisiana, with a capacity of about 8.4 million tonnes per year, backed by Kimmeridge Energy and Mubadala Energy. It has signed long-term offtake agreements with commodity traders and energy buyers. Based in Houston. B2B project developer with almost no public brand awareness.

COX Group is a Spanish company headquartered in Seville that develops water, energy and infrastructure projects, including desalination, solar power plants and green hydrogen across Europe, Africa, the Middle East and Latin America. Its business lines cover engineering, construction and operation of concessions, and it has raised large project financing. Privately held. B2B infrastructure developer with limited consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

CreditAccess Grameen is an Indian microfinance company headquartered in Bengaluru, a leading non-banking financial company providing small joint-liability loans to women in rural and semi-urban areas through branches across more than a dozen states. It serves millions of borrowers with a loan portfolio above 25,000 crore rupees, and is majority owned by CreditAccess Asia, backed by Creation Investments. Listed on NSE and BSE as CREDITACC. Revenue is interest and fees. Regional lender with low urban consumer brand awareness.

Crescent Energy is a Houston-based US independent oil and gas company listed on the NYSE (CRGY), formed in 2021 from KKR-backed Independence Energy and Contango. It owns producing assets in the Eagle Ford, Uinta, Permian, Rockies and Barnett basins, producing roughly 250,000 barrels of oil equivalent daily, and grows through acquisitions, including Vital Energy in 2025. Revenue is oil and gas sales. B2B upstream operator with no public consumer brand.

Cypress Creek Energy is an independent power producer and solar developer based in Durham, North Carolina, previously known as Cypress Creek Renewables. It develops, finances, builds and operates utility-scale solar and energy storage projects across the US, selling power to utilities and corporate buyers under long-term contracts. Founded in 2012, it is backed by private equity firms and lenders. B2B energy developer with little public awareness.

Deutsche Bank is Germany's largest bank, headquartered in Frankfurt, founded in 1870 and listed on the NYSE and Frankfurt exchange (DB). It operates Corporate Bank, Investment Bank, Private Bank and DWS asset management, serving retail, corporate and institutional clients in about 60 countries with roughly 90,000 employees. Revenue comes from lending, trading, advisory and fees. Major global financial brand with a history of sports and cultural sponsorship, including partnerships in golf and football.

Diamondback Energy is an independent oil and natural gas producer based in Midland, Texas, listed on Nasdaq (FANG) and focused on the Permian Basin. It produces around 900,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day after acquiring Endeavor in 2024, and holds mineral interests through subsidiary Viper Energy. Sells to refiners and marketers; revenue exceeds 10 billion dollars. Founded 2007. B2B upstream operator with no consumer brand recognition.

Doha Bank is a commercial bank headquartered in Doha, Qatar, founded in 1979 and listed on the Qatar Stock Exchange. It offers retail, corporate, private and Islamic-style banking, plus trade finance, in Qatar and through branches and representative offices in India, Kuwait, UAE, Turkey and other markets. Revenue comes from lending spreads and fees. Among Qatar's larger private banks. Established local brand with limited global recognition.

Doral Renewables is a US developer, owner and operator of large-scale solar and wind projects, headquartered in Philadelphia and part of the Doral Group with Israeli parent origins. It builds utility-scale solar projects in the US, selling power to utilities and corporate offtakers, and has raised project financing from banks and tax equity investors. B2B renewable energy developer with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

DTE Energy is a Detroit-based diversified energy company listed on the NYSE (DTE). Its DTE Electric and DTE Gas utilities serve about 2.3 million electric and 1.3 million gas customers in Michigan, with additional businesses in renewable energy, energy trading and pipelines. Annual revenue is around 13 billion dollars, mostly regulated utility rates paid by households and businesses. Its Detroit Edison utility dates back to the 1890s. Well-known regional utility brand in Michigan with local sponsorships.

Dubai Aerospace Enterprise (DAE) is an aviation services company headquartered in Dubai, owned by the Investment Corporation of Dubai. It is one of the world's largest aircraft lessors (DAE Capital) with hundreds of aircraft, and also runs engineering and maintenance (DAE Engineering) and a regional MRO. Customers are airlines around the world; revenue comes from lease rentals and MRO services. Founded 2006. B2B aviation business with limited consumer awareness.

Dubai Islamic Bank is the world's first full-service Islamic bank, founded in 1975 and headquartered in Dubai, and the largest Islamic bank in the UAE by assets. It offers Sharia-compliant retail, corporate, wealth and treasury services, with branches across the UAE and operations in Pakistan, Kenya and elsewhere. Customers include individuals, SMEs and corporates; the Investment Corporation of Dubai is a major shareholder. Listed on the Dubai Financial Market. Strong regional consumer brand and an active sponsor in the Gulf.

Duke Energy is one of the largest US electric utilities, headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, and listed on the NYSE (DUK). It supplies electricity to about 8.6 million customers and natural gas to over 1.7 million across the Carolinas, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky, with fleet capacity of roughly 54,000 megawatts. Revenue is about 30 billion dollars from regulated rates. Founded in 1904. Well-known regional utility with local sports and community sponsorships.

EDF Power Solutions, formerly EDF Renewables North America, is the North American renewables arm of French state-owned EDF, based in San Diego, California. It develops, builds, owns and operates wind, solar and storage projects, with over 20 gigawatts developed in the US, Canada and Mexico, and provides asset management and O&M services. Customers are utilities and corporate offtakers. Rebranded as EDF power solutions in 2023. B2B energy developer, brand tied to the larger EDF group.

Emera is a Canadian energy and services company headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia, listed on the TSX (EMA). It owns regulated electric and gas utilities including Nova Scotia Power, Tampa Electric and Peoples Gas in Florida, New Mexico Gas, plus a stake in the Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline, serving about 2.6 million customers. Annual revenue is around 7 billion Canadian dollars from regulated rates. Founded 1998. Regional utility brand with no strong global awareness.

Emirates NBD is a leading banking group in the Middle East headquartered in Dubai, formed in 2007 from the merger of Emirates Bank and National Bank of Dubai, majority owned by Investment Corporation of Dubai. It provides retail, corporate, Islamic and private banking, including Liv digital bank and Network International-linked payments, with operations in UAE, Egypt, Turkey (DenizBank), India and Saudi Arabia. Listed on Dubai Financial Market. Strong regional consumer brand and prominent sponsor of sport and events in Dubai.

EnBW (Energie Baden-Wurttemberg) is one of Germany's largest energy companies, headquartered in Karlsruhe and about 98 percent owned by the state of Baden-Wurttemberg and municipal associations. It generates, trades and distributes electricity, gas and water, operates grids, offshore wind farms and EV charging networks (EnBW mobility+), and serves millions of customers with about 27,000 employees and revenue over 40 billion euros. Founded 1997. Well-known German utility brand; local sports sponsor, including football.

Enfinity Global is a renewable energy developer and independent power producer with roots in Belgium and Italy, now headquartered in Miami, developing solar and storage projects across Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia-Pacific, and with a global project pipeline of several gigawatts. Backed by private equity and lenders, it sells power under long-term contracts to utilities and corporates. Founded in 2007. B2B energy developer with little public brand awareness.

Engie is a French multinational energy and services group headquartered in Paris (La Defense), listed on Euronext Paris (ENGI), with the French state as its largest shareholder. It generates and sells electricity, natural gas and renewable energy, operates networks and offers energy efficiency and building services, with about 97,000 employees and revenue around 70 billion euros, across Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and the US. Formed by the 2008 merger of Gaz de France and Suez. Strong consumer brand in France and Belgium and a sponsor of sport and events.

Entergy Corporation is an integrated electric utility holding company headquartered in New Orleans, listed on the NYSE (ETR). Its subsidiaries serve about 3 million customers in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas, and operate a sizeable nuclear fleet plus Entergy Wholesale Commodities. Revenue is around 12 billion dollars, mostly regulated rates. Founded in 1913. Well-known regional utility with community sponsorships rather than national consumer marketing.

Eos Energy Enterprises designs and manufactures zinc-based battery energy storage systems, with headquarters in Edison, New Jersey and a factory in Turtle Creek, Pennsylvania. Its Znyth aqueous zinc technology targets long-duration storage for utilities, renewable developers and commercial customers, with partners including Talen and Cerberus-linked financing. Listed on Nasdaq (EOSE), still early in revenue and loss-making. Founded 2008. B2B cleantech with limited consumer brand awareness.

Erste Group is a leading Austrian banking group headquartered in Vienna, with about 16 million customers in Austria, Czechia, Slovakia, Romania, Hungary, Croatia and Serbia through brands like Erste Bank, Ceska sporitelna and Slovenska sporitelna. It provides retail, corporate and capital markets banking, with about 45,000 employees and listing on Vienna Stock Exchange (EBS). Founded 1819. Strong consumer brand in Central and Eastern Europe, involved in sports and arts sponsorship.

Eutelsat is a French satellite operator headquartered in Paris (Issy-les-Moulineaux), listed on Euronext Paris (ETL) and, following its 2023 merger with OneWeb, a provider of geostationary and low-earth-orbit connectivity. It sells broadcasting capacity to TV channels, broadband and mobility connectivity to governments, airlines, telcos and enterprises worldwide. The French state became its largest shareholder in a 2025 capital raise to support European sovereign satellite capacity. B2B infrastructure with modest public awareness.

Exchange Income Corporation (EIC) is a Winnipeg-based acquisition-oriented company listed on the TSX (EIF), with two segments: aerospace and aviation (regional airlines Perimeter, Calm Air, PAL Airlines, Canadian charters, aircraft maintenance and special mission aircraft) and manufacturing (Quest, Ben Machine, Water Services, Spartan Bioscience). It serves remote communities, governments and industry across Canada and abroad, with annual revenue above 2 billion Canadian dollars. Founded 2002. Regional airline brands, otherwise a B2B conglomerate.

Expand Energy is the largest US natural gas producer, formed in 2024 by the merger of Chesapeake Energy and Southwestern Energy and renamed from Chesapeake. Headquartered in Oklahoma City and listed on Nasdaq (EXE), it produces over 7 billion cubic feet of gas equivalent per day from the Appalachian Basin and Haynesville shale, selling to utilities, LNG exporters and marketers. Revenue is gas and liquids sales, several billion dollars annually. B2B upstream producer with little consumer brand awareness.

Fanatics is a US sports merchandise and fan engagement company headquartered in New York, selling licensed jerseys, apparel and collectibles for the NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, football clubs and others through its online stores and partner sites. It also operates Fanatics Collectibles (Topps), Fanatics Betting and Gaming, and Fanatics Fest, with a valuation of roughly 31 billion dollars in its 2022 round. Customers are fans and leagues, and it earns from merchandise sales and licensing. Privately held. Very strong consumer sports brand already working with F1 teams and leagues.

Finastra is a London-headquartered financial software company supplying core banking, lending, payments and treasury platforms to banks and financial institutions in more than 100 countries, with about 7,000 employees. Created in 2017 when Misys acquired D+H, it is owned by private equity firm Vista Equity Partners, which sold the Treasury and Capital Markets unit to Apax in 2025. Revenue is software licences, subscriptions and services. B2B with low consumer awareness but strong banking industry presence.

First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB) is the UAE's largest bank, formed in 2017 by the merger of National Bank of Abu Dhabi and First Gulf Bank, and headquartered in Abu Dhabi. It provides corporate and investment, retail, private banking and global markets services across the UAE and international offices in over 20 markets, with assets above 1 trillion dirhams. Partially owned by the Abu Dhabi sovereign Mubadala and ruling family entities; listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange. Strong Gulf brand and a major sports sponsor.

Frontier IP Group plc is a United Kingdom-based company listed as a specialist asset management and consulting firm, headquartered in London. The input describes it as working in asset management and consulting,. The reported funding figure is unclear. Operations, scale and current status are not confirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Galaxy Digital is a New York-based financial services and digital assets firm founded by Mike Novogratz in 2018, offering trading, asset management, investment banking, staking and Bitcoin mining and data centre infrastructure, including AI and high-performance computing hosting in Texas. Clients are institutions and crypto-native businesses; revenue comes from trading, fees and mining. It completed a US listing on Nasdaq (GLXY) in 2025. Business-to-business brand known in crypto circles with limited mainstream consumer awareness.

Gap Inc. is a US apparel retailer headquartered in San Francisco and listed on the NYSE (GAP). It owns Gap, Old Navy, Banana Republic and Athleta, selling clothing and accessories through roughly 3,500 company-operated and franchise stores and online in the US and abroad, with annual revenue around 15 billion dollars. Customers are mainstream consumers; money comes from retail sales. Founded 1969. One of the most recognised fashion brands globally, with large consumer reach and marketing partnerships.

Generate Capital is a San Francisco-based infrastructure investment and operating company founded in 2014 by Scott Jacobs, financing and owning sustainable infrastructure such as solar, battery storage, EV charging, waste-to-energy and water systems, then operating them under service contracts. Customers are corporations, municipalities and developers; it earns long-term service fees. Backed by Blackstone, Temasek, Goldman Sachs and others, with several billion dollars in capital. B2B climate infrastructure with low consumer visibility.

Genesis Energy is a Houston-based midstream master limited partnership listed on the NYSE (GEL). It owns pipelines, offshore Gulf of Mexico crude oil transportation, sodium minerals (soda ash) and trona mining in Wyoming, and marine transportation, serving oil producers, refiners and industrial buyers. Revenue is fees and mineral sales. Founded 1996. B2B energy infrastructure and minerals company with little public brand awareness.

Golar LNG is a Bermuda-based, London-managed provider of floating LNG infrastructure, listed on Nasdaq (GLNG). It owns and operates FLNG vessels such as Hilli Episeyo and Gimi, converting natural gas into LNG offshore for producers in locations like Cameroon and Mauritania/Senegal, and previously owned FSRUs and LNG carriers. Customers are oil and gas companies, paying long-term tolling fees. Founded 2001, linked to Hemen Holding (John Fredriksen). B2B shipping and energy business, no consumer brand.

Greenko Group is one of India's largest renewable energy companies, headquartered in Hyderabad, with wind, solar, hydro and pumped-storage assets across several Indian states and a pipeline of integrated round-the-clock renewable projects. It sells power to state utilities and to commercial and industrial buyers under long-term contracts, and has been funded by investors including GIC, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Orix, with the founders' AM Green taking a larger role from 2024. Founded 2009. B2B power producer with limited public brand recognition.

Grenergy Renovables is a Spanish renewable energy developer and independent power producer headquartered in Madrid, listed on the Spanish stock exchange (GRE). It develops, builds and operates solar parks, wind and battery storage, with core markets in Spain, Chile, Mexico, Colombia, Italy and Germany and a pipeline of many gigawatts. Customers are utilities and corporate buyers; revenue comes from power sales and project sales. Founded 2007. B2B energy firm with little consumer awareness, though known in the Spanish stock market.

GTA Semiconductor is a Shanghai-based Chinese semiconductor manufacturer operating wafer fabrication, with a focus on specialty processes such as power and analog chips and mixed-signal products for the domestic market. It supplies electronics and industrial customers and has raised significant funding from state-linked and private investors. Founded in the 2010s with ambitions to rank among China's leading foundries. B2B chipmaker with almost no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Hydro One is the largest electricity transmission and distribution utility in Ontario, Canada, headquartered in Toronto and listed on the TSX (H). It owns and operates about 30,000 km of high-voltage transmission lines and distributes power to around 1.5 million mostly rural customers. Revenue is regulated rates, roughly 8 billion Canadian dollars. The Province of Ontario retains a minority stake after partial privatisation in 2015. Well-known provincial utility, local community sponsorships only.

Hydro-Quebec is the state-owned electric utility of Quebec, Canada, headquartered in Montreal and owned by the Government of Quebec. It generates mostly hydroelectric power from dozens of dams, exports electricity to the US northeast and Ontario, and serves about 4.5 million customers in Quebec. Revenue is roughly 17 billion Canadian dollars annually. Founded 1944. Among the world's largest hydroelectric producers and a major corporate brand in Quebec, with a presence in arts and sports sponsorship.

ICICI Bank is one of India's largest private sector banks, headquartered in Mumbai (registered in Vadodara), serving retail, SME and corporate customers through roughly 6,500 branches and over 16,000 ATMs, plus mobile apps such as iMobile Pay. It has international branches and subsidiaries in the UK, Canada and Singapore. It also owns ICICI Prudential insurance and mutual fund joint ventures. Founded 1994, listed on NSE, BSE and NYSE (IBN). Very strong consumer brand across India and an existing sports sponsor.

IndiGo (InterGlobe Aviation) is India's largest airline by market share, with over 60 percent of domestic traffic and a fleet of 400 plus Airbus A320 family and ATR aircraft, flying to dozens of international destinations. Headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana, it was founded in 2006 and is listed on the NSE and BSE. It operates a low-cost model with ancillary revenue, and carries around 100 million passengers a year. Strong mass-market consumer brand in India and a large advertiser.

Industrial Bank Co., Ltd. is a Chinese national joint-stock commercial bank headquartered in Fuzhou, Fujian, listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. Founded 1988, it is a significant mid-sized lender with corporate, retail, green finance and financial markets businesses and hundreds of branches across China. Provincial government and state-linked entities are among shareholders. Revenue comes from loan interest and fees. Strong domestic reputation in green finance, though little recognition outside China.

ING Group is a Dutch banking and financial services group headquartered in Amsterdam and listed on Euronext Amsterdam and the NYSE (INGA). It serves around 40 million customers across more than 100 countries with retail and direct banking, notably in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Poland and Australia, plus wholesale banking for corporates. Revenue comes from lending margins and fees, with roughly 60,000 employees. Strong consumer brand in Europe with long track record in sport and cultural sponsorship.

Intesa Sanpaolo is Italy's largest banking group, headquartered in Turin with offices in Milan, formed in 2007 through the merger of Banca Intesa and Sanpaolo IMI. It serves around 13 million customers in Italy through retail, private, corporate and wealth management, with banking subsidiaries across Central and Eastern Europe and Egypt. Listed on Borsa Italiana (ISP) and employing over 90,000 people. Strong Italian consumer brand with extensive sponsorship in arts and sport.

IPX Power is a US power producing company based in Beaverton, Oregon, operating in clean energy and energy storage with a focus on developing and operating renewable generation projects. It sells electricity to utilities and other offtakers, and is privately held. Scale and project list are not confirmed from the input. B2B energy firm with little public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) is a multilateral development financing institution headquartered in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, established in 1973 and owned by around 57 member countries. It finances infrastructure, trade, education and health projects in Muslim-majority countries through Sharia-compliant instruments, with an AAA credit rating and subscribed capital in the tens of billions of dollars. Customers are governments, public agencies and private sector projects. Not a consumer brand; sponsorship interest would be institutional and reputational.

Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) is a Japanese government-owned policy financial institution headquartered in Tokyo, wholly owned by the Government of Japan. It provides export credits, overseas investment loans and project finance to support Japanese companies abroad and strategic resource security, working with commercial banks on infrastructure, energy and manufacturing projects worldwide. Funded by government sources and bonds. Public sector institution, not a consumer brand.

JD Logistics is the logistics arm of JD.com, headquartered in Beijing and listed in Hong Kong (2618) since 2021. It provides warehousing, express delivery, freight and supply chain technology to JD.com and external clients across China and overseas, with hundreds of warehouses and over 500,000 staff including couriers. Revenue is above 150 billion yuan, mainly from logistics services. Founded 2007 inside JD.com. Strong consumer-facing brand in China through deliveries, though largely B2B abroad.

Joby Aviation is a US electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft developer headquartered in Santa Cruz, California, listed on the NYSE (JOBY). It is developing a five-seat piloted air taxi, with Toyota as a major investor and manufacturing partner, Delta Air Lines as a partner, and Uber links through its former Uber Elevate acquisition. It has begun flight tests and pursues FAA certification and launch in Dubai. Founded 2009 and pre-revenue. High-profile technology brand with strong media interest.

Kalshi is a New York-based prediction market exchange regulated by the US CFTC as a designated contract market, letting users trade event contracts on politics, economics, weather and sports. Founded in 2018 by Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara, it scored a major legal win over the CFTC in 2024 and has raised funding at a valuation reported in the billions from investors like Sequoia and Paradigm. Revenue comes from trading fees. Fast-growing consumer fintech with partnerships in sports and media.

Keyera is a Canadian midstream energy company headquartered in Calgary and listed on the TSX (KEY), operating natural gas gathering and processing plants, NGL fractionation and storage, and an iso-octane facility across Western Canada. In 2025 it agreed to acquire Plains All American's Canadian NGL business. Customers are producers and industrial users, paying fees. Founded 1998 from Pembina and others. B2B energy infrastructure operator with little consumer awareness.

Kodiak Gas Services is a US contract compression provider headquartered in The Woodlands, Texas and listed on the NYSE (KGS). It owns and operates one of the largest fleets of natural gas compression units, serving producers and midstream companies mainly in the Permian Basin, Eagle Ford and Haynesville under long-term fee-based contracts. Revenue is around 1.2 billion dollars. Backed by private equity firm EQT before going public in 2023. B2B energy services with no consumer brand.

L3Harris Technologies is a major US defence and aerospace technology company headquartered in Melbourne, Florida, formed in 2019 from the merger of L3 Technologies and Harris Corporation, and listed on the NYSE (LHX). It builds communications, sensors, electronic warfare, space payloads and missile solutions for the Pentagon, allied governments and commercial space customers, with about 47,000 employees and revenue over 21 billion dollars. Revenue comes from government contracts. B2B defence supplier with limited consumer brand awareness.

Legendary Entertainment is a Burbank-based film, television and media company founded in 2000 by Thomas Tull and owned by China's Dalian Wanda Group since 2016. It produces and co-finances blockbusters such as Dune, Godzilla and Kong, the Jurassic World series (as financing partner), plus the Legendary Comics and television arms. Customers are studios, streamers and audiences; revenue comes from film, licensing and distribution. Strong entertainment brand with a track record of branded content partnerships.

Leonardo is an Italian aerospace, defence and security group headquartered in Rome, majority-owned by the Italian government's Ministry of Economy, and listed on Borsa Italiana (LDO). Formerly Finmeccanica, it makes helicopters (AgustaWestland), aircraft, electronics, cyber and space systems, with about 60,000 employees and revenue near 17 billion euros. Customers are militaries, governments and civil operators worldwide. B2B defence brand known in Italy and across industry; sponsorship interest mostly in technology and prestige.

Liberty Media is a US media and entertainment company based in Englewood, Colorado, controlled by chairman John Malone. It owns Formula One Group (Formula 1's commercial rights holder) and a Live Nation stake; the Braves baseball team (split off 2023) and SiriusXM (merged out 2024) no longer sit inside it. Listed on Nasdaq (FWONA/FWONK and others). Revenue is mainly F1 media rights, race promotion fees and sponsorship. Already central to F1.

Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) is India's largest life insurer and investor, headquartered in Mumbai and owned by the Government of India, which listed it through a record IPO in May 2022 on the NSE and BSE. It sells life, pension and savings policies through over 1.3 million agents, with a market share of more than 60 percent in new policies and assets of roughly 50 trillion rupees. Founded 1956. One of India's most trusted household brands and a major advertiser.

Lockheed Martin is the world's largest defence contractor, headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland and listed on the NYSE (LMT). It builds the F-35 fighter, F-16, Black Hawk helicopters, missiles, missile defence and space systems, with about 120,000 employees and revenue near 70 billion dollars, predominantly from the US government and allied militaries. Formed in 1995 from Lockheed and Martin Marietta. B2B and government brand with high recognition but little consumer marketing; it is a known technology partner in motorsport-adjacent engineering.

London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) is a global financial markets infrastructure and data company headquartered in London and listed on the LSE (LSEG). It operates the London Stock Exchange, LCH clearing, FTSE Russell indices and, since acquiring Refinitiv in 2021, the Workspace and Eikon data platforms, serving banks, asset managers and corporates worldwide with about 25,000 employees and revenue above 8 billion pounds. Microsoft holds a stake. B2B financial brand with high professional recognition.

Macquarie Group is an Australian global financial services group headquartered in Sydney and listed on the ASX (MQG), operating in about 30 markets with roughly 20,000 employees. Businesses cover asset management (Macquarie Asset Management), banking and financial services, commodities and global markets, and Macquarie Capital advisory. It owns and invests in infrastructure and renewable assets, with annual income around 17 billion Australian dollars. Founded 1969. Strong corporate brand, with sponsorship history in Australian sport and events.

Masdar (Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company) is a state-owned renewable energy company headquartered in Abu Dhabi, owned by TAQA, Mubadala and ADNOC. It develops and operates solar, wind and green hydrogen projects in over 40 countries, targeting 100 GW of capacity by 2030, and runs Masdar City, a sustainability-focused urban development. Customers are utilities and governments. Founded 2006 and a host of the COP28 climate talks in Dubai in 2023. B2B with strong government and sustainability brand profile.

Matrix Renewables is a renewable energy platform headquartered in Madrid, owned by institutional investors, developing solar and storage projects in the US, Spain, Chile, Mexico, Colombia and Peru. It sells power to utilities under long-term contracts and has secured large project financing. B2B energy developer with limited consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

MidOcean Energy is a global LNG company formed in 2023 by EIG, an energy investment firm, as a platform for LNG liquefaction and regasification investments. It focuses on acquiring interests in LNG liquefaction and related gas assets. Headquartered in Washington, DC, it is privately owned and sells LNG to utilities and energy traders. B2B energy investor with no consumer profile.

Mizuho Financial Group is one of Japan's three megabanks, headquartered in Tokyo (Otemachi) and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and NYSE (MFG). It operates Mizuho Bank, Mizuho Trust and Mizuho Securities, serving individuals, corporations and institutions in Japan and around 35 countries with roughly 60,000 employees. Revenue comes from lending, securities and asset management. Formed in 2000 from the merger of Dai-Ichi Kangyo, Fuji and Industrial Bank of Japan. Strong Japanese consumer brand with sport and cultural sponsorships.

National Australia Bank (NAB) is one of Australia's big four banks, headquartered in Melbourne and listed on the ASX (NAB). It serves around 10 million customers with personal, business and corporate banking, wealth management and institutional banking in Australia and New Zealand (BNZ), and has a large business banking franchise. Founded 1858 with about 38,000 employees. Strong consumer brand in Australia and an existing sports and cultural sponsor, including the AFL.

National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) is an Indian government-owned development financial institution headquartered in Mumbai, set up by an Act of Parliament in 2021 to fund long-term infrastructure projects such as roads, power, ports and railways. It lends to project developers and issues bonds, with equity from the Government of India. Operating since 2021. Public sector financier with no consumer brand profile.

Naturgy is a Spanish integrated gas and electricity utility headquartered in Madrid, listed on the Spanish stock exchange (NTGY). It supplies natural gas and electricity to around 15 million customers in Spain, Latin America and elsewhere, operates networks and renewable power generation and has a large global LNG business. Revenue is roughly 22 billion euros. Formerly Gas Natural Fenosa, renamed 2018. Major shareholders include CVC, GIP and Criteria Caixa. Established consumer energy brand in Spain with football and sports sponsorships.

NatWest Markets is the investment banking arm of NatWest Group, based in London, providing rates, currencies, financing and debt capital markets services to corporate, institutional and public sector clients in the UK and Europe. It was restructured after the 2008 financial crisis to be smaller and ring-fenced from retail banking, as part of the UK government-linked NatWest Group, which is listed on the LSE (NWG). B2B markets business; parent NatWest is a major consumer brand and sports sponsor.

New Fortress Energy is a US energy infrastructure company headquartered in New York, listed on Nasdaq (NFE), that builds LNG terminals, floating storage and regasification units and gas-fired power plants, selling LNG to power plants and industrial users in the Caribbean, Latin America, Brazil and elsewhere. Founded 2014 by Wes Edens, it has expanded through Hygo and GasLog deals and ownership of fast LNG projects. Revenue is around 2 billion dollars; financially stressed in 2025. B2B energy firm with no consumer brand.

Nexamp is a Boston-based developer, owner and operator of distributed solar and battery storage projects, focused on community solar and commercial rooftops in the US Northeast and Midwest. Founded in 2007 and later backed by Blackstone and Brookfield infrastructure investors, it sells clean power to utilities, businesses and subscribers who receive bill credits. Dozens of projects totalling more than a gigawatt. Customer-facing brand in community solar states, with low national awareness.

Nexstar Media Group is the largest US local television station owner, headquartered in Irving, Texas and listed on Nasdaq (NXST), with over 200 stations reaching about 39 percent of US households, plus national cable network NewsNation and The CW. Revenue is around 5 billion dollars from retransmission fees and advertising, including political ads. Founded 1996. In 2025 it agreed to acquire Tegna. Audience-facing media company with large reach among US local viewers, relevant for advertising.

NextEra Energy is a major US energy company based in Juno Beach/Palm Beach, Florida and listed on the NYSE (NEE). Its regulated utility Florida Power & Light serves around 6 million customer accounts, while NextEra Energy Resources is the world's largest generator of wind and solar power, with large battery storage and nuclear operations. Revenue is roughly 25 billion dollars. Customers are households, utilities and corporate buyers. Founded in 1925. Strong utility brand in Florida; sponsors sports and community events there.

NIIF Infrastructure Finance Limited (NIIF IFL) is an Indian infrastructure financing non-bank financial company based in Mumbai, sponsored by the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund, which is backed by the Government of India and global investors. It provides long-term loans and debt to roads, renewable energy, ports and urban infrastructure projects. Customers are infrastructure developers and project companies. Formerly IDFC Infrastructure Finance. B2B financial company with no consumer profile.

NiSource is a US regulated utility holding company headquartered in Merrillville, Indiana and listed on the NYSE (NI). Through NIPSCO and Columbia Gas companies it delivers natural gas and electricity to about 4 million customers in Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Kentucky and Maryland, with annual revenue near 5.5 billion dollars. It also invests in renewable generation. Founded 1912. Regional utility brand with local sponsorships only.

OCBC Bank (Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation) is the second-largest bank in Southeast Asia by assets, headquartered in Singapore and listed on the Singapore Exchange (O39). It provides consumer, SME and corporate banking, wealth management through Bank of Singapore, and insurance via Great Eastern, with a network across Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Greater China and others. Founded 1932 through a merger of three banks. Strong consumer brand in Singapore with a long history of sports and community sponsorship, including cycling and golf.

Ontario Power Generation (OPG) is the Ontario provincial government-owned electricity generator, headquartered in Toronto. It operates nuclear stations (Darlington and Pickering), large hydroelectric plants including Niagara Falls, and biomass and solar, producing roughly half of Ontario's electricity, and is developing small modular reactors at Darlington. Revenue is regulated and contract prices, about 7 billion Canadian dollars. Created from Ontario Hydro in 1999. Strong provincial brand, mainly public sector with local community sponsorships.

Orbital Space Technology is a Beijing-based commercial aerospace company developing satellites and related space systems, including remote sensing small satellites and data services for commercial and government customers in China. The listed funding indicates significant private investment in China's commercial space sector. Operating status and revenue are not confirmed. B2B space company with low consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Origis Energy is a Miami-based developer and independent power producer of utility-scale solar and battery storage, with more than 20 GW of pipeline and operating projects across the United States, and a presence in Europe and Latin America. Founded 2011 by Johan Vanhee and Frank Hoynck, it sells power to utilities and corporates under long-term contracts. Backed by Antin Infrastructure Partners; the founder-led team has raised billions in project finance. B2B energy brand with little consumer awareness.

Palantir Technologies is a US software company founded in 2003, listed on Nasdaq (PLTR) and long headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with the input showing a Miami base. Its Gotham, Foundry and AIP platforms integrate and analyse data for governments, defence and intelligence agencies and large enterprises across health, energy and industry. Revenue exceeds 3 billion dollars annually, growing with AI adoption. B2B brand with strong media and investor profile, and some F1 and commercial partnerships.

Peabody Energy is the largest private-sector coal producer in the United States, headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri and listed on the NYSE (BTU). It mines thermal coal for power utilities and metallurgical coal for steelmakers at operations in the US and Australia, with annual revenue near 4 billion dollars. Founded 1883. Customers are power generators and steel manufacturers. B2B mining company with limited public recognition outside the energy and mining industries.

Ping An Bank is a Chinese national joint-stock commercial bank headquartered in Shenzhen, majority-owned by the Ping An Insurance group and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (000001). It offers retail banking, credit cards, wealth management, SME and corporate banking through hundreds of branches, with a strong fintech and cross-selling focus within the Ping An ecosystem. Revenue comes from loan interest and fees. Its parent is a household name in China, with extensive sports sponsorship, including football.

Power Finance Corporation (PFC) is an Indian government-owned non-banking finance company headquartered in New Delhi, listed on the NSE and BSE. It provides loans and financing to state utilities, generation companies and renewable power projects, and also owns REC Limited. Loan assets run into the trillions of rupees. Founded 1986 and owned majority by the Government of India. B2B financier with low consumer profile.

Qatar Islamic Bank (QIB) is Qatar's largest Islamic bank, headquartered in Doha and listed on the Qatar Stock Exchange (QIBK). It offers Sharia-compliant retail, corporate and wealth banking, with subsidiaries and affiliates abroad. Founded 1982, with the Qatari state and royals among shareholders. Strong national consumer brand and sponsor of sports and cultural events in Qatar.

QatarEnergy, formerly Qatar Petroleum, is the state-owned oil and gas company of Qatar, headquartered in Doha, and one of the world's largest LNG producers with capacity of 77 million tonnes a year, being expanded to about 142 million. It also operates upstream fields, petrochemicals, fertilisers and shipping, and holds international stakes in projects such as Golden Pass LNG. Founded 1974; wholly owned by the Government of Qatar. B2B energy giant, a long-time sponsor of sport and events in the Gulf.

Recurrent Energy is the US-based solar and storage developer owned by Canadian Solar, headquartered in Austin, Texas after relocating from San Francisco. It develops, owns and operates utility-scale solar and battery projects, with a global pipeline of tens of gigawatts and operations in North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific. Customers are utilities and corporate buyers under power purchase agreements. Founded 2006; Canadian Solar acquired the business in 2015. B2B energy developer, brand tied to its parent.

Rheinmetall is a German defence and automotive supplier headquartered in Dusseldorf, listed on the Frankfurt exchange (RHM) and a DAX member. It makes ammunition, armoured vehicles (Lynx, Boxer, Panther), air defence systems and military trucks for NATO armies, plus automotive parts. With about 30,000 employees, revenue passed 9 billion euros in 2024 and is rising on European rearmament. Founded 1889. It sponsors Borussia Dortmund, giving the brand visibility in European football and rising public awareness.

Riyad Bank is one of Saudi Arabia's largest banks, headquartered in Riyadh and listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul). Founded 1957, it provides retail, corporate, treasury, Islamic and private banking through a network of branches and ATMs across the Kingdom, with international arms in London, Houston and Singapore and a stake in Riyad Capital. The Public Investment Fund and GOSI-linked institutions are major shareholders. Strong Saudi consumer brand and an active sponsor of football and sports events.

Rowan Digital Infrastructure is a Denver-based developer and operator of hyperscale and AI data centre campuses, seeking low-cost, renewable-powered capacity in the US. It builds large-scale facilities for cloud and AI tenants, aiming for industrial campuses with on-site power. Private and backed by institutional investors. B2B infrastructure company with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

RTE (Reseau de Transport d'Electricite) is France's electricity transmission system operator, headquartered in La Defense near Paris and owned by EDF (50.1 percent), CDC and CNP Assurances. It runs about 105,000 km of high-voltage lines, balances supply and demand and manages cross-border interconnections, with roughly 9,000 employees and revenue around 6 billion euros from regulated tariffs. Created 2000. Critical-infrastructure B2B brand known to the French public through Ecowatt alerts, but not a consumer marketer.

RWE is a German energy company headquartered in Essen, listed on the Frankfurt exchange (RWE) and a DAX member. It generates power from offshore and onshore wind, solar, hydro, gas and battery storage, is one of the world's largest offshore wind operators, and trades energy; the coal and nuclear exit is under way. Employs about 20,000 people, with revenue around 25 billion euros. Founded 1898. Customers are utilities and industry; consumer retail now largely handled elsewhere. Well-known German brand with football sponsorship history, including Bundesliga links.

Saudi National Bank (SNB), headquartered in Jeddah, is Saudi Arabia's largest bank by assets, created in 2021 by the merger of National Commercial Bank (NCB) and Samba Financial Group. It provides retail, corporate, treasury, wealth and Sharia-compliant banking, with branches in Saudi Arabia and offshore operations. The Public Investment Fund holds around 37 percent. Listed on the Saudi Exchange. Strong consumer brand in the Kingdom, including football and event sponsorships such as the Saudi Pro League.

SB Energy is a US renewable energy developer and operator owned by SoftBank Group, headquartered in San Francisco. It develops large solar and battery storage projects across the US, particularly Texas, and was part of OpenAI's Stargate data centre power effort. In 2025 it got a major investment linked to OpenAI. It sells power to utilities and corporates. Founded 2016 as SoftBank Energy. B2B energy business with limited consumer visibility but a high-profile parent.

Sharjah Islamic Bank is a Sharjah-based bank in the United Arab Emirates, offering Sharia-compliant retail, corporate and SME banking, finance and investment products through branches in the emirate and the wider UAE. Government of Sharjah entities are major shareholders; it is listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange and grew from the former National Bank of Sharjah. Revenue is financing profit and fees. Regional bank with moderate consumer recognition in the UAE.

Shield AI is a defence technology company founded in 2015 and headquartered in San Diego, California, building the Hivemind AI pilot software and V-BAT and Nova drones that operate without GPS or communications. Customers are the US Department of Defense, special forces and allied militaries; revenue is contracts and software. It has raised several hundred million dollars at a valuation of several billion dollars. B2B defence brand known in the military and tech press, not a consumer brand.

Silver Lake is a large technology-focused private equity firm founded in 1999, headquartered in Menlo Park, California with offices in New York, London, Hong Kong and elsewhere. It manages over 100 billion dollars across buyouts and growth investments in Dell, Endeavor, Qualtrics and other companies, and raises money from pension funds and endowments, earning management and carry fees. Co-owner of Manchester City's City Football Group stake and owner of a stake in Endeavor, so it has existing sports exposure. Institutional brand.

Sirius XM is the US satellite and online audio entertainment company, headquartered in New York and listed on Nasdaq (SIRI). It sells subscriptions to music, talk and sports channels on SiriusXM, Pandora and Stitcher to roughly 33 million subscribers, mainly in cars, with revenue around 8.5 billion dollars. Liberty Media was its controlling shareholder until the 2024 merger of Liberty Sirius into SiriusXM. Founded 1990s. Strong US consumer brand with extensive sports and music programming, including NASCAR and NFL content.

Solaris Energy Infrastructure, formerly Solaris Oilfield Infrastructure, is a Houston-based company listed on the NYSE (SEI) that began with mobile proppant management systems for US shale drillers and now provides mobile gas-fired power generation for oil and gas operators and data centres, building a fleet of several hundred megawatts to over 1 GW. Customers are exploration and production companies and AI data centre developers; revenue is equipment rental and services. Founded 2014. B2B energy infrastructure with no consumer profile.

STAG Industrial is a US real estate investment trust headquartered in Boston and listed on the NYSE (STAG) that owns single-tenant industrial and warehouse properties, mostly in secondary markets. It holds roughly 600 buildings totalling over 100 million square feet, leased to logistics, manufacturing and e-commerce tenants. Revenue is rent, around 700 million dollars. Founded 2010. B2B property owner with no consumer brand.

StandardAero is a Scottsdale, Arizona aircraft engine maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) provider for business jets, helicopters, military and commercial aircraft, serving operators and engine makers like Honeywell, GE and Rolls-Royce. It has facilities across North America, Europe and Asia and about 7,000 employees, with revenue around 5 billion dollars. Owned by Carlyle until its NYSE listing (SARO) in October 2024. B2B aerospace services with limited public awareness.

Starwood Property Trust is a large US commercial real estate finance company and mortgage REIT, headquartered in Greenwich, Connecticut with operations from San Francisco, listed on the NYSE (STWD). It originates and invests in commercial mortgage loans, infrastructure lending and property investments. Managed by affiliates of Starwood Capital Group and Barry Sternlicht. Founded 2009. Customers are property owners and developers; B2B financier with low consumer profile.

Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG) is one of Japan's three megabanks, headquartered in Tokyo and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and NYSE (SMFG). It runs Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, SMBC Nikko Securities, SMBC Consumer Finance and Sumitomo Mitsui Card, with large operations in Asia and stakes in Jefferies and Indian lender Yes Bank. Employs more than 100,000 people. Founded 2002. Strong Japanese consumer brand and a major sponsor in sport and culture, including golf and tennis.

Sunoco LP is a Dallas-based master limited partnership listed on the NYSE (SUN) and one of the largest US wholesale motor fuel distributors, supplying around 10,000 convenience stores, independent dealers and commercial customers across more than 40 states. It also owns terminals and pipelines, including the NuStar assets acquired in 2024. Revenue is more than 20 billion dollars, mostly pass-through fuel sales. Managed by Energy Transfer. Sunoco-branded fuel is also known to US drivers and a long-time NASCAR race fuel supplier.

Sunrun is the largest US residential solar company, headquartered in San Francisco and listed on Nasdaq (RUN). It installs rooftop solar and home batteries, selling mainly through long-term leases and power purchase agreements, and serves over 1 million customers. Revenue is above 2 billion dollars, plus subscription income, and it also owns solar assets financed by investors. Founded 2007. Consumer-facing brand in states like California, Arizona and the Northeast, advertised via TV and partnerships.

Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD Bank Group) is one of Canada's Big Five banks, headquartered in Toronto, with large US operations as TD Bank, America's Most Convenient Bank. It offers retail, commercial, wealth, insurance and capital markets services to over 27 million customers, and is listed on the TSX and NYSE (TD). Assets exceed 2 trillion Canadian dollars and it has about 100,000 employees. Founded 1955. Strong consumer brand across Canada and the US east coast, with large sponsorships including TD Garden.

Transocean is a Swiss-based offshore contract drilling company with its registered office in Zug and operating headquarters in Switzerland and Houston, listed on the NYSE (RIG). It owns and operates a fleet of ultra-deepwater and harsh-environment drilling rigs and drillships, hired by oil majors and national oil companies. Revenue is day-rate contracts, around 3 billion dollars. Founded 1973. B2B oilfield services company with no consumer brand.

United Group is a multi-play telecoms and media provider in Southeast Europe, headquartered in Hoofddorp in the Netherlands and controlled by BC Partners. It operates mobile, broadband and pay-TV in Serbia (SBB), Bulgaria (Vivacom), Slovenia, Croatia, Montenegro and Bosnia, and owns N1 news and Nova TV channels plus sports rights. Millions of subscribers across the Balkans. Privately held, with debt-financed acquisitions. Strong regional consumer brand and sports broadcaster, so a potential media partner.

United Overseas Bank (UOB) is one of the three Singapore banking groups, headquartered in Singapore and listed on the Singapore Exchange (U11). It provides personal, SME, corporate, wealth and private banking across Southeast Asia (Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam) and Greater China, with over 500 branches. Founded 1935. Employs about 28,000 people, with annual income around 14 billion Singapore dollars. Strong consumer brand in Southeast Asia, a major arts and sports sponsor in Singapore.

United Wholesale Mortgage (UWM) is the largest US wholesale mortgage lender, based in Pontiac, Michigan and listed on the NYSE (UWMC). It originates home loans only through independent mortgage brokers, not directly to consumers, funding well over 100 billion dollars of loans yearly, and it has barred brokers who also work with rival Rocket Mortgage. Founded 1986, controlled by CEO Mat Ishbia, who also owns the NBA Phoenix Suns. B2B mortgage brand, with some consumer visibility through sports sponsorships.

USA Compression Partners is a Texas-based master limited partnership listed on the NYSE (USAC), providing natural gas compression services on fee-based contracts to producers, gatherers and processors in the Permian, Marcellus and other shale basins. It has one of the largest compression fleets in the US at roughly 3.7 million horsepower, and is controlled by Energy Transfer. Revenue is about 900 million dollars. Founded 1998. B2B energy services firm with no consumer brand.

Vedanta is a diversified Indian natural resources group in the Anil Agarwal family, with Vedanta Resources in London and operating Vedanta Limited listed in India, headquartered in Mumbai. It produces zinc, lead, silver, aluminium, copper, iron ore, oil and gas and steel in India, Africa and Namibia, with revenue of roughly 17 billion dollars. Its subsidiary Hindustan Zinc is the world's largest integrated zinc producer. Founded 1976. Mainly B2B; Cairn and Hindustan Zinc and others sponsor sport. A 2025 demerger split the group into several listed units.

Vertical Bridge is the largest private owner and operator of wireless towers in the United States, headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida, with about 400 employees and more than 30,000 towers. It leases tower space and rooftop sites to carriers such as AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile, as well as building new sites. Backed by Digital Colony, and it bought Verizon's tower portfolio in 2024. Founded 2014. B2B infrastructure with no consumer visibility.

Victory Capital is a US asset management firm headquartered in San Antonio, Texas, listed on Nasdaq (VCTR), that owns multiple independent investment franchises and manages around 300 billion dollars in mutual funds, ETFs and separate accounts. It sells through financial advisers and institutions and has grown by acquiring firms such as USAA Asset Management and Amundi US. Founded as a KeyCorp unit and independent since 2013. B2B financial brand with low consumer awareness.

Viper Energy is a Midland, Texas-based mineral and royalty company, a subsidiary of Diamondback Energy, listed on Nasdaq (VNOM). It owns royalty interests in Permian Basin oil and gas land, receiving a share of production without bearing drilling costs, and has expanded with acquisitions including Sitio Royalties in 2025. Revenue is royalties, around 1 billion dollars. Formed 2014. B2B energy royalty vehicle with no consumer profile.

VoltaGrid is a Houston-area (Bellaire, Texas) company that provides mobile, modular natural-gas-fired power generation for oilfields, data centres and industrial users, delivering power as a service. It has supply agreements with large AI and cloud customers and has raised large funding rounds and large data centre power agreements. Founded 2022. B2B power provider with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Wabash Valley Resources is an Indiana energy company in West Terre Haute that is developing a coal-gasification plant converting petroleum coke and coal into ammonia, with carbon capture and storage to produce low-carbon fertiliser and hydrogen. It has raised investment from energy and infrastructure funds and secured federal support. Customers would be fertiliser and industrial buyers. B2B project developer with no public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Western Midstream Partners is a Texas master limited partnership based in The Woodlands, listed on the NYSE (WES) and sponsored by Occidental Petroleum. It gathers, processes and transports natural gas, crude oil and produced water for producers in the Delaware Basin, DJ Basin and other regions, with revenue near 3.5 billion dollars. Fee-based contracts with Occidental and others. Formed 2008 as Anadarko Midstream. B2B energy infrastructure with no consumer brand.

Yangtze Memory Technologies Corporation (YMTC) is a Wuhan-based Chinese maker of 3D NAND flash memory chips, founded in 2016 and backed by the Big Fund, Tsinghua Unigroup and local government investors. It supplies solid-state drives and smartphone memory, including the Xtacking architecture products, and was placed on the US Entity List in 2022. Customers are device makers and the Chinese electronics industry. It sells the Zhitai consumer SSD brand in China, otherwise B2B.

Yes Bank is an Indian private sector bank headquartered in Mumbai, founded 2004 and listed on NSE and BSE. After a 2020 collapse and RBI-led rescue involving SBI, ICICI and others, it was restructured and in 2025 Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation took a large stake of about 20 percent. It offers retail, SME and corporate banking, digital payments and trade finance across India with over 1,000 branches. Recognisable Indian consumer brand and an existing sponsor of cricket and tennis events.

Yinson Production is the floating production storage and offloading (FPSO) arm of Malaysian group Yinson Holdings, headquartered in Singapore. It owns and operates FPSOs on long-term charters in Ghana, Brazil, Angola, Nigeria and Asia for oil majors and national oil companies. The Yinson Holdings parent is listed on Bursa Malaysia, controlled by the Lim family. B2B offshore energy services with no consumer profile.

Zenobe Energy is a UK-based developer and operator of grid-scale batteries and electric vehicle fleet charging and battery leasing, headquartered in London. It builds large battery storage sites for the electricity grid and finances electric bus depots and fleets for operators such as Transport for London bus operators. Founded 2017. Backed by institutional infrastructure investors. B2B energy storage company with limited consumer awareness but strong UK clean energy profile.

Zurich Insurance Group is a Swiss multinational insurer headquartered in Zurich and listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (ZURN). It provides property and casualty, life and commercial insurance to individuals, SMEs and large corporates in more than 200 countries and territories, with about 60,000 employees and revenue over 70 billion dollars. Founded 1872. Strong global insurance brand with existing sports sponsorship, including football, cycling and the Zurich Classic of New Orleans golf event.

Arch Capital Group is a Bermuda-based specialty insurance, reinsurance and mortgage insurance company listed on Nasdaq (ACGL). It writes property, casualty, specialty and mortgage insurance and reinsurance through Lloyd's syndicates and offices in the US, UK, Europe and Canada, serving businesses and other insurers. Revvity is a US life sciences and diagnostics company headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts and listed on the NYSE (RVTY), the former PerkinElmer after it sold its analytical and services units in 2023.
